report.summary: Reviewed canary.py chunk 1 of 5: module docstring claims and constants; all checkable claims kept at this level, several require later chunks.
risks: canary.py:1-109 | medium | Module docstring claims about subprocess environment, synthetic payload, and no repo reads cannot be verified in this chunk; later chunks must confirm. | Check chunks 2-5 for council_env usage, probe body construction, and any file reads.

canary.py:130-132 | low | CANARY_STATUSES is documented as CLOSED, but the enforcement (no sixth member) is not visible in this chunk; later code may add members. | Verify no other assignments to CANARY_STATUSES in this file.

canary.py:157-160 | low | FAILING_STATUSES excludes 'unavailable' as documented, but the exit-code logic that uses it is not in this chunk; a mismatch could invert the policy. | Check run_canary and exit_code in later chunks.
canary.py:170-176 | low | VENDOR_KEYS is claimed to match council.session.VENDOR_KEYS; this chunk cannot see council.session, so the claim is uncheckable. | Compare with council/session.py.

canary.py:178-181 | medium | REPLY_TRIM=400 is claimed to prevent history.jsonl from becoming a transcript store; the actual truncation logic is not in this chunk. | Verify to_record or append_history trims to REPLY_TRIM.
canary.py:183-189 | low | SLOWER_RATIO and SLOWER_ABS_S are claimed to be used conjunctively; the comparison logic is not in this chunk. | Check compare_to_history.
canary.py:194-198 | low | new_nonce is claimed to be fresh PER PROBE PER LANE; the call sites are not in this chunk. | Verify probes_for or run_canary calls new_nonce per lane.

canary.py:204-210 | low | _rng is claimed to be deterministic so build/check agree; the actual use in build/check functions is not in this chunk. | Check build_arrival and check_arrival in later chunks.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, imports, __all__, constants, nonce and RNG helpers.

symbols.name: CANARY_STATUSES
symbols.note: Closed tuple of probe outcomes: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error.

symbols.name: SEVERITIES
symbols.note: Tuple of severity levels: liveness, quality.

symbols.name: FAILING_STATUSES
symbols.note: Frozenset of statuses that count as failure: wrong_answer, timeout, error.

symbols.name: VENDOR_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of vendor keys: anthropic, openai, google, local.

symbols.name: _NONCE_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching NONCE- followed by 8 uppercase alphanumerics.

symbols.name: new_nonce
symbols.note: Returns 'K' + 7 uppercase hex chars from secrets.token_hex(4).

symbols.name: _TAIL_WORDS
symbols.note: Tuple of 10 tail words, disjoint from filler words.

symbols.name: _ANCHOR_SETS
symbols.note: Tuple of six 3-tuples of fruit names.

claims.text: EVERY PROBE IS (prompt, checker) AND THE CHECKER IS DETERMINISTIC PYTHON. No model judges another model's answer.
claims.why: The probe builders and checkers are defined later in the file; this chunk only contains constants and helpers, so the claim cannot be verified here.

claims.text: unavailable ... is NOT a failure and never trips the exit code
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES includes 'unavailable' and FAILING_STATUSES excludes it, but the exit-code logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: CANARY_STATUSES is closed
claims.why: The tuple is defined here, but closure (no other assignments) cannot be confirmed without seeing the rest of the file.

claims.text: CanaryRun.summary reports the two groups separately, by construction
claims.why: CanaryRun and its summary method are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: arrival and instruction ask ... that is LIVENESS, and a regression there is an alarm
claims.why: The probe builders and severity assignments are defined later in the file.

claims.text: anchoring and comprehension ask ... that is QUALITY ... does NOT trip the exit code
claims.why: The probe builders and exit-code logic are defined later in the file.

claims.text: every host is passed EXPLICITLY per call; this module never sets, mutates or exports OLLAMA_HOST into any process environment
claims.why: No code that sets environment variables appears in this chunk; the subprocess environment is attributed to vendors.council_env in another module.

claims.text: only 127.0.0.1/localhost counts as local
claims.why: The local-host predicate is imported from session.live_egress_seats, not defined here.

claims.text: every probe body is synthetic -- generated filler, fruit names and invented one-line summaries
claims.why: The probe builders are later in the file; this chunk only defines the corpora constants, not their use.

claims.text: there is no code path here that reads a repo file
claims.why: No file-reading code appears in this chunk; later chunks may contain such code.

claims.text: Transport is not reimplemented: daedalus.council.vendors already puts the prompt on stdin, kills the whole process tree on timeout, strips OLLAMA_HOST and refuses an over-budget Ollama prompt
claims.why: The vendors module is imported but not examined; this chunk does not contain the adapter logic.

claims.text: run_canary takes live and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE
claims.why: run_canary is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Any lane still carrying a shipped vendor transport raises LiveCanaryRefused before a thread is started, before a probe is built and before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: The enforcement logic is in run_canary, not in this chunk.

claims.text: The classification is session.live_egress_seats -- IMPORTED, not re-implemented
claims.why: Line 110 imports live_egress_seats from .session, matching the claim.

claims.text: live_egress_lanes only maps a Lane back to the adapter(s) behind its ask callable and hands them to that one function
claims.why: live_egress_lanes is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The operator's form is daedalus canary --live. Without it the CLI refuses and points at --dry-run; --dry-run prints the plan, calls nothing, and NAMES THE SEATS --live would call
claims.why: The CLI entry point is not in this chunk.

claims.text: --live --dry-run together is REFUSED as ambiguous
claims.why: The CLI logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Outcome of one probe. CLOSED -- nothing may invent a sixth
claims.why: The tuple is defined with five members, but closure requires seeing the rest of the file.

claims.text: unavailable and wrong_answer are separate members because a report that merges them is a report that lies
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES includes both 'unavailable' and 'wrong_answer' as distinct strings.

claims.text: A probe either measures whether the lane is ALIVE and the bytes arrived, or whether the lane's reasoning is the right SHAPE. Only liveness trips the exit code
claims.why: SEVERITIES is defined, but the binding of probes to severities and the exit-code logic are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Statuses that mean 'we asked and it did not work'. unavailable is deliberately absent
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES = frozenset({'wrong_answer', 'timeout', 'error'}) does not include 'unavailable'.

claims.text: Dumb, append-only, no database
claims.why: The path is defined, but the append-only behaviour is in append_history, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Cheapest sensible local model. This runs often; the 32b is not a health check, it is a bill.
claims.why: DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL is set to 'qwen2.5-coder:7b', which is a 7b model, not 32b.

claims.text: Vendor keys, spelled the way the operator types them (same set as council.session.VENDOR_KEYS so --vendors means one thing repo-wide).
claims.why: VENDOR_KEYS is defined here, but council.session.VENDOR_KEYS is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Enough to see what a lane actually said, not enough to turn history.jsonl into a transcript store.
claims.why: REPLY_TRIM is defined, but the trimming logic is in later code (to_record or append_history).

claims.text: Long enough to be a baseline, short enough that a lane which legitimately got faster stops being compared against last month.
claims.why: TRAILING_WINDOW is defined, but the comparison logic is in compare_to_history, not this chunk.

claims.text: A lane counts as materially slower only if it is BOTH a large multiple of its median AND absolutely slow enough for a human to care. Either test alone cries wolf
claims.why: SLOWER_RATIO and SLOWER_ABS_S are defined, but the conjunction logic is in compare_to_history.

claims.text: Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer
claims.why: new_nonce is defined and returns a fresh random value, but the per-probe-per-lane call pattern is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Deterministic per-nonce randomness, so build and check agree
claims.why: _rng is defined deterministically, but the build/check functions that use it are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Disjoint from _FILLER_WORDS on purpose: the arrival tail token must not be findable anywhere in the padding
claims.why: The sets of words in _FILLER_WORDS and _TAIL_WORDS are disjoint; no word appears in both.

claims.text: None of these describes a real file in this repo, and none of them may contain 'roll'/'revert'
claims.why: The comment is cut off; the summary list is not fully visible, and repo file names are not known.

observations.what: The module docstring claims several enforcement properties (no OLLAMA_HOST mutation, synthetic payloads, no repo reads) that cannot be verified in this chunk; they depend on later chunks or other modules.
CANARY_STATUSES is documented as CLOSED, but the enforcement (no later additions) is not visible in this chunk.
FAILING_STATUSES excludes 'unavailable' as documented, but the exit-code logic that uses it is not in this chunk; a mismatch could invert the policy.
VENDOR_KEYS is claimed to match council.session.VENDOR_KEYS; this chunk cannot see council.session, so the claim is uncheckable.
REPLY_TRIM=400 is claimed to keep history.jsonl from becoming a transcript store; the actual truncation logic is not in this chunk.
SLOWER_RATIO and SLOWER_ABS_S are claimed to be used conjunctively; the comparison logic is not in this chunk.
new_nonce is claimed to be fresh PER PROBE PER LANE; the call sites are not in this chunk.
_rng is claimed to be deterministic so build/check agree; the actual use in build/check functions is not in this chunk.
